The first `

The `` element is missing the required `alt` attribute. Screen readers have nothing to read, and the image provides no fallback text if it fails to load. Add a descriptive alt: `alt="Our team photo"`, or `alt=""` if the image is purely decorative.

title: Using b Instead of strong
code: Please read the terms and conditions before continuing.

bugs.explanation: `` is presentational with no semantic meaning. For text that is important, use `` instead — screen readers may stress it, and search engines give it semantic weight. Replace `` and `` with `` and ``.

The Home link uses `href="#"`, which scrolls to the top of the page instead of navigating anywhere. This is a placeholder that was never filled in. Replace with the actual path: `href="/"` or `href="/home"`.

The `<input>` is missing a `type` attribute. Without it browsers default to `type="text"`, but intent is unclear. For an age field, `type="number"` is correct — it enables numeric keyboards on mobile and allows `min`/`max` validation. Always specify `type` explicitly.

`margin: auto` for horizontal centering only works on block-level elements. `<span>` is inline by default and ignores auto margins. Add `display: block;` to the rule, or switch to a block element like `<div>`.

`z-index` has no effect on elements with `position: static` (the default). The `.tooltip` has no `position` set, so `z-index: 100` is ignored and the tooltip may appear behind other elements. Add `position: relative;` (or `absolute`/`fixed`) to activate the stacking context.

title: Percentage Width With No Parent Width

bugs.explanation: A percentage `width` is calculated relative to the containing block. If `.sidebar`'s parent has no explicit width (e.g. is absolutely positioned without one), `.sidebar` can collapse to 0. Ensure the parent has a defined width, or use a fixed unit like `px` or `vw`.

title: Duplicate id Attribute
code:
<form>
  <input id="email" type="email" placeholder="Primary email">
  <input id="email" type="email" placeholder="Backup email">
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>

bugs.explanation: `id` values must be unique within a page. `document.getElementById('email')` returns only the first match, CSS selectors behave unpredictably, and accessibility tools can malfunction. Use a unique id like `id="backup-email"` on the second input.

The `<form>` is missing both `action` and `method` attributes. Without `action`, the form submits to the current URL. Without `method`, it defaults to `GET`, which appends form data to the URL — a security risk for login forms. Add: `action="/login" method="POST"`.

title: Label for Doesn't Match Input id

bugs.explanation: The `<label>`'s `for="user-email"` does not match the `<input>`'s `id="email"`. This breaks the label-input association: clicking the label won't focus the input, and screen readers won't correctly announce the label. Fix: change `for` to `"email"` or change the input `id` to `"user-email"`.

`color` sets the foreground (text) color, not the background. To give `.alert` a yellow background, use `background-color: #ffeb3b;`. As written, the element will have yellow text on whatever the inherited background is.

A `<script>` tag in `<head>` without `defer` or `async` blocks HTML parsing — the browser stops building the DOM until the script downloads and executes. Add `defer`: `<script src="/js/app.js" defer></script>`. This executes the script after the DOM is parsed without blocking rendering.

title: display none vs visibility hidden (No Bugs)

bugs.explanation: The data rows are direct children of `<table>`, skipping `<tbody>`. While browsers implicitly insert one, omitting it is bad practice: `table > tr` CSS selectors won't match, and some JavaScript DOM operations targeting `<tbody>` will fail. Wrap the data rows in `<tbody>...</tbody>`.

title: CSS Specificity Bug

bugs.explanation: `p.highlight` has lower specificity than `#main-content p`. An ID selector outweighs any number of class selectors, so `.highlight` paragraphs inside `#main-content` appear grey, not red. Fix by increasing specificity: `#main-content p.highlight { color: red; }`.

title: Missing charset Meta Tag
code: Hello, world!

bugs.explanation: The `<head>` is missing `<meta charset="UTF-8">`. Without it, browsers guess the encoding, causing special characters and emoji to render as garbled symbols. Add `<meta charset="UTF-8">` as the first element inside `<head>`, before `<title>`.
